sources.title: Huawei OD interview note containing the heap-class prompt
Answer Batch 0019 mechanically extracted repository-source packet
Deterministic Java validation against PriorityQueue plus direct heap invariant checks
Source-first isolated review for the heap-class candidate

claims.text: The retained repository source asks to abstract a heap as a class and implement retrieval/deletion operations, without specifying min/max orientation, language, API names, duplicate policy or empty-heap behavior.
Java int min-heap semantics, add/peek/poll names, duplicate support, input-copy construction and exceptions on empty access are explicit candidate choices rather than source facts.

For the chosen min-heap representation, add restores parent<=child order by sifting the appended value upward, while poll replaces the root with the last value and restores order by sifting downward through the smaller child.
The implementation provides O(1) peek, O(log n) add/poll, O(n) bottom-up array construction and O(n) storage for n elements.
The executable candidate supports duplicate and extreme int values, rejects null array construction, throws on empty peek/poll and does not mutate the caller's constructor array.
The exact Java fixture passes 10 fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized operation sequences against java.util.PriorityQueue while checking parent<=child after every operation.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=10 randomized=5000 oracle=java-priority-queue heap=min duplicates=supported empty=throws mutation=input-none
checks: 5000 deterministic randomized operation sequences against java.util.PriorityQueue
heap parent<=child invariant after every random operation and drain

boundary_tests.expected: poll order remains nondecreasing with repeated values preserved
bottom-up heapify produces correct order without mutating caller input
all observable results match PriorityQueue and every internal snapshot satisfies parent<=child

findings: The candidate remains bounded to the heap-class source prompt and labels all concrete API choices.
The implementation and PriorityQueue oracle agree across fixed and randomized operation sequences.
The answer explains the parent/child invariant and why insertion/deletion only require one repair path.
Complexity, duplicate handling, empty behavior and input non-mutation claims match the executable artifact.
Formal promotion remains blocked only by the required human-approval gate.
